newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen recovering slightly at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen recovering slightly at open.

* Toronto stocks were expected to open a bit higher, recovering ground lost in the past two session. * Analysts said trading would remain cautious ahead of Monday's election.

Toronto stocks were expected to open stronger on Thursday, recouping some of the losses of the past two sessions, but analysts said the market would remain cautious ahead of Monday's general election.

"I think we're going to open on the plus side and get a bit of a recovery today...the TSE has had two days of heavy declines and I think it's time for a bit of a rebound," said technical analyst Katherine Beattie at MMS International.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 53.51 points on Wednesday to close at 6389.03. The exchange has shed more than 100 points over the past two days.
Beattie said significant gains were unlikely as investors remain skittish ahead of the Canadian June 2 federal election.

"The market is going to remain cautious, especially the Canadian dollar, ahead of Monday's election, so I don't think we're going to get a strong bounce, but I do think we could enjoy a positive day," she said.

Recent opinion polls which show slightly decreased support for the governing Liberals has added volatility to the currency market but the Canadian dollar improved overnight and bonds and bills were up modestly.
Beattie said the financial sector, which has been badly hit over the past couple of days, should be able to recover some ground as associated markets strengthen.

"The banks have reported strong profits over the past couple of days and the reason they've been down is the negative activity in our bill and bond market. And because those markets are rebounding today, that sector should do well," she said.

In economic news from Statistics Canada, the preliminary estimate of average weekly earnings for Canadian workers in all industries except agriculture and fishing rose 2.7 percent in March from a year earlier to a seasonally adjusted C$594.68.
From the month before, earnings fell 0.3 percent.
Seasonally adjusted payroll employment rose 0.2 percent or 18,000 employees in March to 11.18 million from 11.16 million in February.
The number of Canadians applying for employment insurance benefits in March rose 0.7 percent to 228,000 from February.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Toronto-Dominion Bank and National Bank of Canada were expected to release second-quarter earnings later in the session. Earnings from Canada's big six national banks have so far met analysts' expectations.
